title: push endpoint SSRF: validates URL but follows internal DNS
description: push.rs:264-268. The push notification sender validates the endpoint URL via validate_outbound_url, which checks for private IP addresses and non-HTTPS schemes. However, as noted in federation.rs:60-63, DNS rebinding is NOT mitigated. An attacker could register a push subscription with an endpoint URL that resolves to a public IP during validation, then re-resolves to 169.254.x.x or 10.x.x.x during the actual POST. Since push notifications carry server-generated payloads (not user-controlled), the SSRF impact is limited to network scanning/probing rather than data exfiltration. This is the same DNS rebinding issue documented for federation but with a different attack vector.
close_reason: Already documented as accepted risk in federation.rs:60-63. Same DNS rebinding vector as federation, same mitigation status.
